#77364. Tech Report: Western Brands Need a Fresh China Playbook

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2323 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Western Brands Need a Fresh China Playbook

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2323 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Western luxury in China has hit serious roadblocks in recent years.
  • Industry observers note that “I think the relationship between Chinese consumers and Western brands is undergoing a significant shift,” says Cherry Xu, founder of Shanghai-based fashion-art foundation Cheruby.
  • The latest round of earnings revealed that China’s luxury market is taking longer to stabilize than hoped.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Western luxury in China has hit serious roadblocks in recent years. The old approach of opening stores and investing in top-down marketing is now ineffective, as local consumers look elsewhere for authenticity and clear value propositions. And so, the brands that rise to the challenge by localizing their output, optimizing distribution, and adapting to China’s new consumer will be best placed when the market recovers.

Industry observers note that “I think the relationship between Chinese consumers and Western brands is undergoing a significant shift,” says Cherry Xu, founder of Shanghai-based fashion-art foundation Cheruby. “Younger generations no longer automatically associate Western origins or heritage with greater value.”.

The latest round of earnings revealed that China’s luxury market is taking longer to stabilize than hoped. According to Bain’s report released early this year, the mainland Chinese personal luxury market contracted 3-5% in 2025. And although it displayed signs of recovery in the second half of the year, fashion, specifically, is still struggling. “There have been quite a few [Chinese] store closures, and I think the mood is unsupportive of luxury,” Goldman Sachs luxury analyst Erwan Rambourg told Vogue Business in October.

In a recent development, “The third quarter brought a more challenging Chinese consumer backdrop with a ‘feel-good’ factor deteriorating at the very beginning of the quarter,” LVMH CFO Cécile Cabanis stated during the group’s earnings call in October. Until June, Hermès was growing in Greater China, but is now broadly flat year-on-year following the Q3 results due to a decline in traffic. Kering declined 8% in the Asia-Pacific region, excluding Japan. CEO Luca de Meo said in a statement that “delivering our action plan in China” will help the group to restore momentum. At Prada Group, too, China remained a weak point.

“Weaker consumer confidence, slower economic growth, and heightened price sensitivity are weighing on discretionary spending, following more than a decade in which China was a key driver of global luxury growth,” stated Fflur Roberts, head of luxury goods at Euromonitor International.

Sources indicate that in recent years, domestic brands have shone in China by embracing their native understanding of Chinese cultural sensibilities and offering better value for money, as consumers show heightened price sensitivity — a significant drag on the discretionary spending that once drove major growth for global luxury players. Local brands are especially well placed to adapt to the rising “Guochao” (direct translation: “national tide”) movement, which incorporates traditional Chinese style elements into contemporary styles.

Sources indicate that chinese luxury consumers continue to engage with Chanel, despite a sluggish market. Pictured: Shan Yichun.

Additionally, Western luxury brands must increasingly compete with a shift in China’s premium consumption. China International Capital Corporation’s (CICC) vice president Liwei Hou reports that overall tenant sales at Chinese high-end malls outperformed luxury brand growth in 2025 and 2026. “Sportswear (Arc’teryx, Salomon) and affordable brands (like Ralph Lauren), as well as Chinese brands (Laopu, Songmont), and fine dining have been the star performers in these high-end malls,” she says. “A crisis of luxury is an opportunity for others. Proactive changes are needed.”.

Until Western brands audit their approach — a time-consuming and complex process — domestic Chinese brands may continue to capture market share, analysts agree, capitalizing on the cost-effective manufacturing infrastructure at their fingertips, which makes room for bigger margins.

For starters, Western brands must adapt to the leading consumer. Experts agree that the commercial backbone for luxury brands in China is the established millennial and Gen X clients, particularly for bigger-ticket purchases.

In Bain’s 2025 report on China’s personal luxury goods market, the firm found that consumer motivations for buying luxury had shifted away from signaling status to a more refined appreciation and discernment. “The Chinese consumer hasn’t stopped spending. They’ve stopped overpaying for a logo. Status has moved from visible wealth to taste, craft, and wellbeing,” claims Jonathan Travers-Smith, CEO of Hotpot, an agency bringing Western brands into East Asian markets. Brands must demonstrate real craft, a credible story and prices that feel earned, Travers-Smith advises. “Some Western houses have priced their way out of that conversation, raising prices year after year while the in-store experience stayed the same.” In addition, he argues, brands should halt price hikes and invest in clienteling.

“The industry has spent a lot of time talking about creativity and marketing, but I think the bigger challenge is rebuilding a sense of value,” says Thomas Chauvet, Citi’s head of luxury goods research. Simply lowering prices is not the answer, he believes. Rather, brands must develop stronger products, better assortments, greater differentiation, and a clearer reason for consumers to buy.

Industry observers note that burberry’s approach to China is working well, confirmed CEO Joshua Schulman on the investor call earlier this month. Greater China’s retail growth grew (5%) in Q2 of fiscal 2026, carried by local spending. This followed a 9% climb in Q1. “We clearly understand that the market in China is challenging right now,” stated Schulman. “That said, we are pleased with our outperformance in a dynamic market. And this has been going on for several quarters.” The brand, he revealed, had risen to the challenge over the last two years, aligning pricing with consumer expectations — aware that globally, and in China especially, consumers were fatigued by exorbitant price points. “This was a historic positioning that we had,” said Schulman. “And coming back to this sweet spot in the luxury market has been a priority for us. We see that this is resonating strongly with our Chinese consumers.”.

The Western brands that are performing have renewed desire through fresh ideas, centered on experiences, travel, beauty and wellness, not just novelty for novelty’s sake. “Creative leadership is central to this process. Matthieu Blazy’s appointment at Chanel offers an example of how a new creative direction can introduce a fresh perspective to an established house and generate renewed consumer interest,” says Julio Ng, co-founder of brand development consultancy 2034. It’s understood that Chanel is performing well in China, despite the downturn for other players.

Ralph Lauren is another outlier. Brand CEO Patrice Louvet told investors earlier this month that China sales remained strong in Q2, increasing more than 35%, bolstered by store sales as well as distribution expansion. Its output remains rooted in premium American style that’s more affordable than most luxury players, resonating with value-conscious Chinese consumers.

In a recent development, “What Chanel and Ralph Lauren do particularly well is that they both have a very distinct sense of world-building,” says Xu. “Chanel has established a cultural presence beyond fashion through art, cinema, and creative expression, while Ralph Lauren offers an entire lifestyle and aesthetic universe.” She argues that both remain true to their identities while creating different entry points into their worlds, noting that brands wanting to build lasting brand value need a clear identity, compelling products, and a consistent creative vision.

Sources indicate that ralph Lauren grew China sales more than 35% in the last quarter. Pictured: Actor Kevin Chu.

Calvin Wang, a luxury and retail consultant, is dubbing it the shift to “rational indulgence”. He explains that VICs should be respected as connoisseurs. “Approach clients with the understanding that they often know more and have seen more than the brand’s frontline staff,” he claims. Wang encourages a focus on UHNWIs to handle the K-shaped economy, where the top end of the economy grows, but the lower end lags as inequalities widen. However, he still recommends maintaining connections to upper-middle-class consumers by offering products of demonstrable quality and longevity.

“When it comes to what brands can control, I think that the focus has to be on reigniting product desirability, so investing in marketing and in innovative retail experience should be the priority,” states Carole Madjo, luxury goods analyst at Barclays.

Industry observers note that in the past, international brands have struggled to land a successful localization strategy in China, often oversimplifying the process. “A China strategy cannot simply be an adaptation of global marketing materials,” says Olivia Chen, co-founder of Shanghai-based brand agency 2034. “Local teams need sufficient understanding of the brand, as well as the authority to make decisions that respond to the market. At the same time, local activity needs to remain aligned with the brand’s international positioning.” Chen sees it as a balancing act. If a Western brand becomes too localized, it loses the qualities that first made it attractive — that is, what the brand represents beyond China.

Industry observers note that “With the increasingly global circulation of information and culture, younger generations are developing their own sensibilities and identities at the intersection of global culture and local experience,” says Xu. “Rather than approaching Chinese consumers as a distinctly separate audience, brands are engaging with individuals who have both a global cultural perspective and their own local experiences. I think this is changing the way we understand localization.”.

Industry observers note that burberry’s localization approach? “Combining our British luxury heritage with locally relevant product and storytelling,” noted Schulman on the brand’s most recent investor call. “In the second quarter, we had capsule collections for Chinese Valentine’s Day, and we also had a localized activation with China National Geography. All of those show our appreciation for and understanding of the local customer.”.

In a recent development, to this day, major brands still produce red-colored Lunar Latest Year collections. But they should “avoid superficial ‘Guochao’ tokenism,” warns Wang. “Designing literal Chinese-themed capsules — such as applying zodiac animals or traditional calligraphy onto Western silhouettes — frequently reads as opportunistic and patronizing. Chinese luxury consumers already look to domestic designers for authentic cultural expression.”.

Equally, brands must develop strong strategies beyond local celebrity endorsements and seasonal campaigns. Travers-Smith takes a hardline on this. “Listen before you spend. Go deep into Xiaohongshu and Douyin for insights into how consumers actually talk about your category, your product, and competitors,” he says. “Build one or two cultural moments a year that are made in China — not adapted for China.” He also encourages empowering an on-the-ground China digital team to make decisions, embrace faster content cycles, and cater content based on different market needs across cities.

In a recent development, for a Western luxury house, Burberry is outperforming in the China market thanks to effective localization. Pictured: Actor Wu Lei.

Travers-Smith pinpoints a massive misconception that Chinese social media is a channel for pushing campaigns. The reality? “It’s where consumers decide what to buy, and Xiaohongshu is a search engine for taste. Building beautifully polished brand-owned content should be the second priority after ensuring your brand is communicated through UGC from influencers and key opinion leaders (KOLs).”.

It has been revealed that as for product assortment and store networks, brands should streamline, Bismuth recommends. This means closing underperforming stores, moving away from promotional activity, and slowing down on retail expansion. This shift is already underway. Louis Vuitton, Dior, Loro Piana, and Tiffany opened new flagship stores in Tier-1 cities while scaling back presence in Tier-2 and Tier-3 locations over recent years. Nonetheless, some insiders favor a more selective approach over a blanket Tier-1-only strategy. One core takeaway experts agree on: treat China as a continent made up of several unique territories.

Recent findings suggest that western companies must also take stock of their wholesale and direct-to-consumer (DTC) networks. “Brands need people who understand their positioning and can represent them in a way that supports their long-term ambitions,” notes Chen. “China is a complex market to navigate, and a brand’s reputation can be affected by how and where its products are sold.”.

It has been revealed that the Chinese DTC landscape is fundamentally different from the rest of the world’s. Discovery, communication, and client relationships are built predominantly on platforms like WeChat’s mini-programs (sub-applications often used for e-commerce) and Tmall Luxury Pavilion (a premium e-concession platform). “Brands must focus on connecting and aligning the distinct strengths of each platform to create a seamless consumer journey,” claims Wang.

Sources indicate that because of the macro downturn and the growing maturity of a relatively new major market, analysts struggle to outline a recovery timeline for Western luxury in China. One thing is clear: brands should not wait it out. “The slump might be cyclical, but the change in behavior is structural,” states Travers-Smith. “Property wealth isn’t coming back to 2021 levels, and the consumer who learned to buy less and better isn’t going to unlearn it.”.

Sources indicate that the smartest players will address issues the boom hid and strategize for potential market disruptors. “For 2027, watch AI. Assistants like Doubao and Qwen are becoming the first place people ask what to buy,” warns Travers-Smith. “If your brand isn’t described accurately and favorably in those answers, you’re invisible at the moment of consideration.”.

In a recent development, in the mid to long-term, luxury houses should also ramp up their knowledge and insights on Chinese Gen Z and Gen Alpha. “[They] are expected to become vital pillars for businesses in 10-20 years, and it is never too early to start understanding them and interacting with them,” indicates Hou. Even today, the Gen Z contingent might not drive direct revenue, but they can give brands cultural relevance.

China’s Gen Z isn’t a core consumer yet, but Western brands should continue to court the group. Pictured: Actor Wang Yibo.

“I would love to see more brands move beyond cultural marketing and towards cultural production. This could mean building long-term relationships with local artists, designers, and independent cultural institutions, supporting research, commissioning newly introduced work, and encouraging cross-disciplinary exchanges,” indicates Xu. “These investments may take longer to develop, but they have the potential to create value for both the brand and the local cultural ecosystem.”.

For Western brands, waiting it out is not a viable option. It’s an expensive mistake. Chauvet encourages action: “Chinese luxury demand may recover, but I suspect the market that emerges will be more mature and more competitive than the one brands enjoyed over the past decade.”.

Thanksgiving Cornbread

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, traditionally, cornbread stuffing requires making cornbread, cubing it and letting it dry out, mixing it with stock, eggs, meat, and aromatics, then transforming it into a stuffing (or dressing). This process produces some truly memorable casseroles, but I have an alternative that streamlines the process without compromising flavor: stuffing cornbread. It still smells enticingly like the classic Thanksgiving side as you set the baking dish on the table. I’ve still packed in a medley of woodsy herbs, sweet onions, vegetal peppers, and savory sausage. And it still slices into lofty servings to perch on your plate next to the sweet potatoes and green beans. It just takes half as long to make.

According to recent reports, the intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins. The sugar might seem like a lot, but it balances out the savory sausage and aromatics perfectly.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a 13x9" baking pan with parchment paper, leaving generous overhang on long sides. Coat pan and parchment with unsalted butter. Melt ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat, then pour into a small bowl.

Cook 1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped, 1 medium white onion, finely chopped, and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, in same skillet, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 1 lb. spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and cook, breaking up and stirring occasionally, until browned (it may still be a little raw in the center at this point), about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

According to recent reports, stir together 4 cups (624 g) fine-ground yellow cornmeal, 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 1 cup (200 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 tsp. baking soda, and ¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary in a large bowl. Gradually pour in 3½ cups buttermilk, then melted butter, stirring constantly until combined. Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition. Fold in sausage mixture, then scrape batter into prepared pan.

Recent findings suggest that bake cornbread, rotating pan front to back halfway through, until golden brown and top springs back when gently pressed, 38–45 minutes. Let cool in pan 15 minutes. Using parchment paper overhang, lift cornbread out of pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into 12–18 slices; arrange on a platter.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Cornbread can be baked 4 hours ahead. Store at room temperature; cut just before serving.

#77362. Is Cottage Cheese Good for You?

Is Cottage Cheese Good for You?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tasteofhome

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yes, cottage cheese is good for you!
  • I have to admit: I can see why cottage cheese recipes go viral.
  • According to recent reports, as a dietitian and recipe developer, I love an ingredient that’s not only nutritious but also versatile and affordable, and that can help me meet my daily protein goals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Yes, cottage cheese is good for you! It's packed with protein and calcium, but the kind you buy matters. Here's how to choose the best cottage cheese for cooking, baking and snacking.

I have to admit: I can see why cottage cheese recipes go viral. TikTok trends have turned this humble dairy staple into everything from high-protein flatbread to better-for-you ice cream. Packed with protein and important vitamins and minerals, cottage cheese is an easy way to make everyday meals more satisfying.

According to recent reports, as a dietitian and recipe developer, I love an ingredient that’s not only nutritious but also versatile and affordable, and that can help me meet my daily protein goals. There are so many creative ways to use cottage cheese, and a whole new world of options opens up when you whip it smooth. Think: smoothies, creamy dips, pasta sauces, puddings and more!

But as versatile as cottage cheese is, you can’t swap it into every recipe without a little know-how. And with so many milkfat options, the one you buy matters. I’ll share my favorite ways to use it, which varieties work best for different dishes and a few tricks to help you get delicious results every time.

First things first: Here’s why you might want to toss another tub of cottage cheese into your grocery cart.

Recent findings suggest that cottage cheese is one of my go-to high-protein foods. A half-cup serving packs 12 to 14 grams of protein, roughly the same amount you’d get from two large eggs.

Adding a scoop of cottage cheese to my plate is an easy way to make meals and snacks more satisfying without turning on the stove. I especially like it at breakfast, when it’s all too easy to end up with a meal that’s heavy on carbohydrates but light on protein. A scoop alongside toast and fruit, or blended into pancake batter, gives breakfast a little extra staying power without much effort.

You don’t have to be lifting heavy weights to care about muscle health. Our bodies need plenty of protein to maintain and repair muscle tissue, and that becomes especially important as we get older.

Recent findings suggest that I like to keep cottage cheese on hand for an easy post-workout snack because there’s nothing to prep. Pair it with fruit or whole-grain crackers, and you’ve got protein plus carbohydrates to help muscles refuel and recover after exercise.

The protein in cottage cheese does more than help keep you full and support your muscles—it also plays an vital role in keeping your bones strong. Cottage cheese aprovides two minerals that work together to support bone health: phosphorus and calcium.

It has been revealed that it’s worth noting that cottage cheese contains less calcium than a serving of milk or Greek yogurt, but it can absolutely contribute to your daily intake. Just be sure to include other calcium-rich foods in your diet, too.

Emiko Franzen For Taste Of Home.

Industry observers note that the type of cottage cheese you buy can make a big difference in how your recipes turn out. Like other dairy products, cottage cheese comes in different milkfat percentages, which affects its taste and texture.

I usually reach for 2% or 4% cottage cheese, depending on how I’m using it. Low-fat (2% cottage cheese) is perfect for whipping into dips, spreads and pasta sauces. It contains enough fat to blend smooth and creamy without feeling too heavy.

Industry observers note that full-fat, or 4% cottage cheese, gets my vote for baked goods, casseroles and lasagna fillings. The extra fat adds richness, which is especially helpful if you’re using it in place of sour cream or cream cheese.

According to recent reports, I usually skip fat-free cottage cheese for cooking. It tends to be watery with a slightly chalky taste, and the lack of fat can make creamy recipes less satisfying. That extra moisture can also affect the texture of baked dishes, so I prefer cottage cheese with a little more fat for the best results.

Sources indicate that for all its nutritional perks, cottage cheese can also pack a lot of sodium. Some brands contain more than 400 milligrams per half-cup serving. Eat a full cup, and you could be getting more than 800 milligrams of sodium (about one-third of the recommended daily limit) from cottage cheese alone.

Too much sodium can raise blood pressure and increase your risk of heart disease, so it’s worth paying attention to how much you’re getting, especially if you eat cottage cheese regularly.

If you’re watching your sodium intake, compare labels and choose a brand that’s lower in sodium. Good Culture is one of my favorite cottage cheese brands. With 380 milligrams of sodium per serving, it’s a little lower than other brands.

I also go easy on added salt when using cottage cheese with salty ingredients like Parmesan or ranch seasoning.

Julia Hartbeck for Taste of Home.

Longtime West Virginia Sen. Rockefeller dies

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockefeller IV, D-W.Va., questions witnesses during a Senate Finance hearing on health care on June 23, 2011.
  • In a recent development, former Sen.
  • Rockefeller, who retired after the 2014 elections, played key roles on the tax-writing Senate Finance Committee, where he helped write landmark children’s health insurance legislation, as well as the Commerce, Science and Transportation and Intelligence panels which he chaired.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. John D. Rockefeller IV, D-W.Va., questions witnesses during a Senate Finance hearing on health care on June 23, 2011. (Scott J. Ferrell/CQ Roll Call).

In a recent development, former Sen. Jay Rockefeller, a five-term West Virginia Democrat and champion for the rural poor, has died at the age of 89.

Rockefeller, who retired after the 2014 elections, played key roles on the tax-writing Senate Finance Committee, where he helped write landmark children’s health insurance legislation, as well as the Commerce, Science and Transportation and Intelligence panels which he chaired.

Recent findings suggest that A staunchly progressive lawmaker, he represented a deeply conservative state that turned further to the right in his later years. Rockefeller, scion of a famous Fresh York family renowned for its wealth, never wavered in his convictions and retired rather than face a potential backlash from voters upset by the then-Obama administration’s attempts to rein in the coal industry.

Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., who challenged Rockefeller for his seat before he decided not to seek reelection, released a statement Friday praising her predecessor’s legacy.

Sources indicate that “Jay dedicated his life to serving West Virginia and our nation, leaving a lasting legacy. He was always a true gentleman who treated me with respect, kindness, and encouragement,” Capito said. “Over the years, we developed a wonderful friendship that transcended politics, and I will always be grateful for that.”.

West Virginia’s Republican Gov. Patrick Morrisey — himself a transplanted Northerner, with roots in Brooklyn and New Jersey — lauded Rockefeller’s record on health care and aid for coal miners and veterans in their adopted state.

“His work helped shape our state and left a lasting mark on the lives of generations of West Virginians,” Morrisey noted.

According to recent reports, rockefeller was born in Latest York City on June 18, 1937, the great-grandson of Standard Oil Co. founder John D. Rockefeller, who was once considered the world’s richest man. Rockefeller attended Harvard University, graduating with an A.B. in 1961. His passion was for the Far East and he spent three years studying at the International Christian University in Tokyo.

Sources indicate that he returned to the states and was appointed by President John F. Kennedy to the National Advisory Council of the Peace Corps in 1961, spearheaded the Peace Corps initial program in the Philippines. He worked for a brief time in what was then known as U.S. Department of Far Eastern Affairs before deciding to embark on a public service role of a more personal nature. He enrolling as a VISTA volunteer, in the program which would later be known as AmeriCorps, and moved to the small mining community of Emmons, W.Va., in 1964 at age 27.

In West Virginia, Rockefeller found his life’s work. He described the experience as being “reborn,” and spoke often the poverty and hardship he encountered living in the small town. “I could not leave,” he said of West Virginia. “I [had] become so devoted to those people and the unfairness.".

According to recent reports, he had planned to remain only one year, but decided to stay and became active in local politics. He broke from his family's long tradition of Republican loyalty and ran successfully for the House of Delegates as a Democrat in 1966. Two years later, he was elected secretary of state.

Rockefeller lost a bid for governor in 1972, but he became the president of West Virginia Wesleyan College and continued to place roots in the state. He married Sharon Percy Rockefeller in 1967 and they started their family. When he ran for governor again in 1976, he won, and served two terms before winning election to the U.S. Senate in 1984, ultimately serving five terms before retiring in 2014.

Sources indicate that rockefeller was determined to increase economic opportunities for West Virginia, for whom he felt was forgotten and abandoned by the rest of the country. He called the people of his state “the hardest-working people I know,” and believed that bringing more business opportunities would help lift the state out of severe rural poverty and the dependence on the coal industry.

It has been revealed that rockefeller traveled to Japan and worked tirelessly to bring a Toyota manufacturing plant to Buffalo, W.Va, one of over twenty Japanese companies he’d brought to West Virginia. He fought for fair trade policies and targeted tax relief to protect West Virginia industries such as steel and chemicals.

Coal mining had long been the economic backbone of West Virginia, but Rockefeller felt more must be done to protect miners, many of whom worked in unsafe conditions or fell ill with pneumoconiosis, or black lung disease, after years of inhaling coal dust.

But defying the coal industry came with a political cost. When Rockefeller originally ran for governor in 1972, he had opposed mountaintop mining, also called strip mining, or the practice of removing large amounts of earth and rock in order to access underground seams of coal. When he ran again in 1976, he reversed his position and won.

But even as he ascended to the Senate, Rockefeller remained both friend and foe to the coal industry.

According to recent reports, despite growing up on the Upper East Side of Manhattan, figuratively and literally hundreds of miles away from coal mines, Rockefeller understood its deep roots in West Virginia’s economy and culture. He believed it was the miners — rather than industry — for whom he was defending.

He hung a century-old photo of a coal miner in his Senate office in the Hart building, and would point to the photo and remark to visitors that “this is why I’m here and who I work for.”.

Rockefeller fought to secure pensions for miners, especially as coal companies would file for bankruptcy and immediately restructure to do away with pension intends.

Industry observers note that in 1990, Rockefeller was one of only 11 senators to vote against the bipartisan Clean Air Act, which he felt disadvantaged workers in West Virginia. But those close to him said the decision weighed heavily on him, and Rockefeller privately worried that the lack of such regulations would pollute the air and destroy waterways, the brunt of which would be born by the same disadvantaged people whom he vowed to protect.

It has been revealed that he believed strongly in the deliberative aspects of the legislative process, consuming great amounts of reading material to familiarize himself with the challenges. During a time of increasing partisan rancor, Rockefeller still reached across the aisle to find a willing partner, even when there was not one to be found.

In 2010, as the Environmental Protection Agency’s greenhouse gas regulations were coming to fruition, Rockefeller came up with a compromise to delay implementation for two years.

He viewed himself as a broker between industry interests and the hard working people from coal-states like West Virginia. He had hoped that his years of standing up for coal miners and West Virginia interests would foster enough goodwill among industries primed to oppose any compromise that was less than an all-out rejection of the existing EPA statutes.

Sources indicate that but industry walked away from Rockefeller, preferring a hard-line opposition to EPA regulations, and lobbied other senators to vote against Rockefeller’s measure. Furious, Rockefeller took to the floor of the Senate to denounce the coal industry and its leaders, an unprecedented action for a popular coal-state senator.

Industry observers note that “The reality is that many who run the coal industry today would rather attack false enemies and deny real problems then find solutions,” he said on the Senate floor in June 2012. “Scare tactics are a cynical waste of time, money and, worst of all, coal miners’ hopes. But sadly, these coal operators have closed themselves off from any other opposing voices and few dared to speak out for change — even though it’s been staring them in the face for years.”.

His fury against the coal industry was heard loudly, many speculating that he would retire rather than face reelection.

According to recent reports, he had won reelection to the Senate handily during his five campaigns. In 2008, his final election, he was reelected with nearly 64 percent of the vote. But six months following his fated coal speech, in January 2013, Rockefeller revealed he would retire at the end of his fifth term.

Rockefeller’s legacy may best be known for his fight to expand health care for vulnerable populations, including children, the economically disadvantaged and the elderly. Rockefeller served as one of the chief congressional champions for President Bill Clinton’s proposed health care overhaul, and later he played a critical role and was a loud progressive voice in writing and passing the Affordable Care Act in the Senate.

Rockefeller believed strongly in a public health insurance option, offering it as an amendment in the Senate Finance Committee during the ACA markup. A public-run insurance proposal, he said, would put patients before profits, and help those people, especially West Virginians, with high health care costs and poor coverage who were left “out in the cold.”.

"These are people," Rockefeller mentioned, visibly emotional during his closing arguments to the Senate Finance Committee. "Eleven-year-old kids. These are families, and we have to respect them. And you respect them by giving them a choice.".

Sources indicate that the amendment was rejected. Rockefeller pivoted to strengthening Medicaid and Children’s Health Insurance Program provisions, believing that poor and disadvantaged families could seek refuge within those programs. CHIP had been one of Rockefeller’s signature legislative victories, helping to write that program initially in 1997 and later working on a major expansion that became law in 2009.

Despite his initial concerns and later disappointments — at one time saying publicly he could not support the measure as it stood — he later added his support to the ACA, citing it as a win for all Americans and actively lobbied his colleagues to support it.

Rockefeller was also known for his role on the Senate Intelligence Committee. A former chairman, he was critical of the nation's mismanagement of the Iraq war and clashed frequently with Republicans over the treatment of detainees. After he retired from Congress, Rockefeller served as a distinguished fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations.

Respect for Rockefeller ran deep on Capitol Hill. He was beloved by staff and known as a thoughtful, deliberative lawmaker. He had a fondness for classical music and served as a board member of the Bach Consort, an organization in Washington devoted to the study and performance of the music of Bach and his contemporaries. He admired art and Asian culture, and served as a board member of the Asia Society.

Rockefeller is survived by his wife, Sharon Percy Rockefeller; four children: John D. Rockefeller V, Valerie Rockefeller, Charles Rockefeller and Justin Rockefeller; and nine grandchildren.

Disclosure: the author served as a staffer in Rockefeller’s Senate office from 2009-11.

It will be a miracle if this colorful, festive and irresistibly sweet Hanukkah bark lasts for eight days and eight nights.

According to recent reports, every holiday is sweeter with a tray of festive chocolate bark—and Hanukkah is no exception! This 30-minute Hanukkah bark recipe takes just a handful of ingredients and turns them into the perfect treat for sharing with friends and family as you celebrate the Festival of Lights. The surface is swirled (a lot like our marbled almond roca), and it looks as if a few dreidels were sent spinning over the melted blue candy melts and white chocolate.

Industry observers note that A tray of Hanukkah bark, decorated with an eye-catching array of colorful and shimmering sprinkles, makes a showstopping centerpiece for any Hanukkah dessert table. But it can also be a thoughtful homemade food gift you can pack into tins with a handful of chocolate gelt.

Line a 15x10x1-inch sheet pan with parchment paper.

Add the blue and white candy melts to separate microwave-safe glass bowls, then microwave at 50% power in 30-second increments, stirring after each, until smooth.

Editor’s Tip: If you’re worried about your chocolate setting too swiftly, place the sheet pan in a warm oven while preparing the candy melts. A warm (but not hot) sheet pan keeps the candy melts fluid while you work, making them easier to swirl without the pressure to rush.

Sources indicate that dollop alternating spoonfuls of each color onto the parchment paper in a checkerboard pattern, leaving space between spoonfuls. Use an offset spatula to merge the colors together, then smooth them to a 1/4-inch thickness. Use a knife or wooden skewer to swirl them to create a marbled look.

Immediately sprinkle the candy melts with candy-coated chocolates and assorted sprinkles.

Industry observers note that transfer the pan to the refrigerator and chill the bark until it’s set. Break it into large pieces.

ELLIE CROWLEY FOR TASTE OF HOME.

Store Hanukkah bark in an airtight container at room temperature for one to three weeks.

Absolutely! Hanukkah bark is a great make-ahead treat for the holiday season because it can be stored at room temperature and has a longer shelf life than many other Hanukkah desserts.

Sources indicate that yes, Hanukkah bark freezes well. Break it apart, then store it in an airtight, freezer-safe container for three to six months. Enjoy it straight from the freezer or defrost it at room temperature.

ELLIE CROWLEY FOR TASTE OF HOME.

It has been revealed that white chocolate and candy melts can be finicky and prone to seizing if you warm them too promptly or at too high a temperature. If using a microwave, warm them gently on a low power setting in short increments for the best results. If you’re nervous, you can melt them on the stovetop using a double boiler or a heat-safe bowl set over a saucepan filled with 1 to 2 inches of water. If neither of those suits you, using a slow cooker or a water bath are some other ways to melt chocolate.

Sources indicate that yes, you can dye white chocolate. Use an oil-based or powdered type of food coloring for the best results. Gel and traditional food dyes contain too much water, which will cause the white chocolate to seize and become grainy.

For the most eye-catching look, choose an array of sprinkles with different sizes and shapes. Varying pearl and jimmie sprinkle sizes, paired with specialty sprinkles shaped like stars, menorahs or dreidels add visual interest to the bark.

Industry observers note that while gelt looks attractive on Hanukkah bark, foil-wrapped chocolates are difficult to remove and unwrap once they’ve been adhered to the bark. If you want to add gelt, unwrap the pieces before arranging them on the bark.

Industry News: BA's Best Orecchiette With Sausage and Broccoli Rabe

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, unlike many iconic Italian recipes, this luxurious union of silky broccoli rabe, chile-flecked sausage, garlic, and curvaceous pasta is a weeknight hero.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, unlike many iconic Italian recipes, this luxurious union of silky broccoli rabe, chile-flecked sausage, garlic, and curvaceous pasta is a weeknight hero. You can make it start to finish, in about 30 minutes. The key to successful execution is to go way beyond blanching when it comes to precooking the broccoli rabe in boiling salted water. For tender rabe that melds seamlessly with pasta and sausage, start by separating the thick stems from the rest of the stalks and giving them a head start before adding the rest. It removes any unpleasant bitterness and also means the rabe will cook into the saucy base of browned sausage and sweated garlic in just minutes.

Sources indicate that while orecchiette is the traditional pasta choice, any short pasta will work. Sausage has become a popular addition to the true original Pugliese dish of stewed broccoli rabe with pasta, but a tin of anchovies makes a great substitute for added oomph and intensity.

This recipe is one of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen's definitive takes on iconic dishes.

Cut 2 large bunches broccoli rabe, trimmed, in half crosswise to separate thick stalks from thinner stems and florets. Cook thicker stalks in a medium pot of boiling salted water until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Add thinner stems and florets and cook until all of the broccoli rabe is tender (the tip of a paring knife should slide through the stalks with little to no resistance), about 3 minutes. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet with tongs; let sit until cool enough to handle (no need to squeeze out excess water unless dripping wet). Coarsely chop into bite-size pieces.

Meanwhile, cook 1 lb. orecchiette (little ear-shaped pasta) or other short pasta in a second medium pot of boiling salted water until al dente (or use same pot with fresh salted water). Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Recent findings suggest that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 1 lb. hot Italian sausage, casings removed if needed, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown and nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes. Add 1 head of garlic, cloves separated, peeled, thinly sliced, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, breaking up sausage even finer if needed and stirring often, until garlic is golden brown and softened, 3–4 minutes. Add broccoli rabe and cook, stirring occasionally, until very tender and wilted, about 5 minutes.

According to recent reports, add 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, pasta, and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Cook, stirring often and adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is coated in a clingy sauce. Taste and add some crushed red pepper flakes if desired. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), and stir, adding more pasta cooking liquid a splash at a time as needed to keep sauce smooth and shiny, until incorporated; season with salt.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan.

Breaking: BA's Best Lasagna

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the secret weapon is the meat sauce.
  • Recent findings suggest that one step you can skip: boiling the noodles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This lasagna recipe has “rainy Sunday cooking project” written all over it. Layers of slow-cooked pork-and-beef ragù, silky Parmesan béchamel, and pasta bake into a rich, creamy lasagna Bolognese with a browned top and crisp edges. Make the sauces ahead to break up the work, or settle in for a day of very good kitchen smells.

According to recent reports, the secret weapon is the meat sauce. Why make meatballs only to break them apart? Searing the meat in large balls leaves room for moisture to escape, so you get deep browning instead of a potful of steam. After a long, gentle braise, a potato masher turns them into ragù. Whole canned tomatoes, crushed by hand, give you control over the sauce’s chunky texture.

Recent findings suggest that one step you can skip: boiling the noodles. In side-by-side retests, regular dried lasagna noodles (not no-boil!) produced similar results whether parboiled or layered straight from the box. The ragù and béchamel provide enough moisture to cook the pasta in the oven—as long as every noodle is covered. Spread the sauces to the edges, leaving no dry patches, and making sure the sauce totally covers the top layer of noodles before baking. Round it out with homemade garlic bread and a Caesar salad.

Do I need to buy no-boil lasagna noodles?

Industry observers note that no—use regular dried lasagna noodles, preferably De Cecco. Skipping the boiling step isn’t the same as using noodles labeled “no-boil.” In our original tests, those absorbed too much sauce, leaving the finished lasagna drier than we wanted.

De Cecco Lasagne No.1 Pasta, 16-oz.

Why doesn’t this lasagna have ricotta or mozzarella?

This is a lasagna Bolognese, built around meat ragù and Parmesan-enriched béchamel rather than a separate cheese filling. The béchamel supplies the creaminess, while Parmesan brings salty, nutty flavor. For a less involved version with a cheese filling, try our Cottage Cheese Lasagna.

What’s the best way to split up the work?

Sources indicate that make the ragù one day, then tackle the béchamel, assembly, and baking the next. For an even lighter second day, make both sauces ahead and refrigerate them separately; rewarm the béchamel just enough to loosen it before layering. The ragù can be refrigerated for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months, while the béchamel can be refrigerated for 1 day.

Watch Chris make BA’s Best Lasagna.

It has been revealed that save recipes and plan every week with confidence. Download the app.

Saving this cooking project for another day? We tasted nine brands to find the best frozen lasagna.

Preheat oven to 225°. Mix 2 lb. ground pork and 1 lb. ground beef chuck (20% fat) with your hands in a large bowl; season generously with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, then mix again. Form into about 18 large meatballs (they don’t need to be perfect—you’ll be mashing them later).

Industry observers note that warm 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Working in 2 batches, cook meatballs, turning occasionally and reducing heat if bottom of pot looks in danger of scorching, until browned all over, about 6 minutes per batch. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet as they’re done.

Reduce heat to medium. Add 2 oz. pancetta (Italian bacon) or slab bacon, chopped, to pot and cook, stirring often, until lightly browned and beginning to crisp, about 5 minutes. Add 1 medium onion, finely chopped, 1 celery stalk, finely chopped, 1 medium carrot, peeled, finely chopped, and 6 garlic cloves, sliced, and cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until paste is darkened in color, about 2 minutes.

Add ¾ cup dry white wine and cook, stirring occasionally, until almost completely evaporated, about 5 minutes. Add one 28-oz. can whole peeled tomatoes, crushing with your hands, and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is jammy and reduced by about half, 8–10 minutes. Add 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth and 1 cup whole milk, then return meatballs to pot. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot partially with a lid, transfer to oven, and cook, checking every hour or so to ensure liquid is at a low simmer and adjusting oven temperature as needed, until meatballs are falling-apart tender, 3–4 hours.

It has been revealed that using a potato masher, break meatballs apart and incorporate into liquid (you should have about 8 cups ragù; transfer pot to stovetop and simmer gently to reduce if needed). Taste and season with more salt and black pepper if needed.

Do ahead: Ragù can be made 4 days ahead. Let cool; cover and chill, or freeze up to 3 months.

According to recent reports, melt 7 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in ¼ cup plus 3 Tbsp. all-purpose flour and cook, whisking occasionally, until mixture smells slightly nutty, about 4 minutes. Whisking constantly, add 6 cups whole milk. Increase heat to medium-high and continue whisking until mixture comes to a simmer. Reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook, whisking occasionally, until béchamel thickens, about 4 minutes. Continue cooking, whisking occasionally and adjusting heat as needed to maintain a gentle simmer, until béchamel is smooth and velvety, 8–10 minutes more. Remove from heat and whisk in 4 oz. Parmesan cheese, coarsely grated (about 1 cup), a pinch of cayenne pepper, and a pinch of ground nutmeg. (You should have about 6 cups béchamel.) Season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. Transfer to a large bowl and press plastic wrap directly onto surface; let cool slightly.

Note: You can skip the following boiling step (and save yourself a pot to wash!). In side-by-side retests, the BA Test Kitchen found that regular dried lasagna noodles (not no-boil) produced similar results whether parboiled or layered straight from the box. To use them uncooked, spread the ragù and béchamel all the way to the edges, covering every noodle completely, and make sure the sauce blankets the top layer of noodles before baking.

Sources indicate that if parboiling: Cook 1¼ lb. dried lasagna noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally and separating them so they don’t stick together, until just starting to soften but still snap in half rather than bend when folded; 3 minutes is the magic number. The noodles will be so firm it will just seem all wrong. Using tongs, transfer noodles to a large bowl of cold water to cool. Drain and lay flat in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet, separated by parchment or wax paper.

Recent findings suggest that lightly coat a 13x9", 4–6-qt. glass or ceramic baking dish with extra-virgin olive oil. Spread 1½ cups ragù in dish. Lay a single layer of noodles over ragù (cut or break noodles as needed to fill any gaps). Spoon 1¼ cups béchamel over noodles, spreading in an even layer with a small offset spatula. Top béchamel with 1½ cups of meat sauce. Repeat layering noodles, béchamel, and ragù 3 more times. Top with a fifth layer of noodles and the remaining 1 cup béchamel.

In a recent development, note: For more pasta in every bite, build six layers instead of five. Start with the same 1½ cups ragù on the bottom of the dish, but use 1 cup béchamel and 1¼ cups ragù between the pasta layers. Finish with a sixth layer of pasta and the remaining 1 cup béchamel.

Sources indicate that cover with a lightly oiled piece of aluminum foil and set lasagna pan on a rimmed baking sheet (just to catch drips). Bake lasagna until bubbling gently around the edges, about 1 hour. Remove from oven. Increase oven temperature to 425° and carefully place rack in top of oven. Remove foil from lasagna and continue to bake until top is browned and crisp around the edges, 10–15 minutes longer. Let sit 10 minutes before serving.

Industry observers note that do ahead: Béchamel can be made 1 day ahead; keep chilled. Rewarm just enough to loosen before using. Lasagna can be assembled 1 month ahead; let cool, then cover with plastic and freeze. Let frozen lasagna thaw overnight in fridge before baking.

Editor’s note: This recipe first appeared in our February 2018 issue as part of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen’s definitive takes on iconic dishes. It has been updated with clearer assembly instructions and guidance from additional BA Test Kitchen testing, including the option to skip parboiling regular dried lasagna noodles. Tech Report: The Secret to Better Gravy Is Already In Your Pantry

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tasteofhome

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It only takes a splash to give homemade gravy the rich, savory flavor you're after.
  • Recent findings suggest that there are few things on the Thanksgiving table that people have stronger opinions about than gravy.
  • According to recent reports, making good turkey gravy isn’t particularly complicated, but getting that deep, rich flavor can be tricky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

It only takes a splash to give homemade gravy the rich, savory flavor you're after.

Recent findings suggest that there are few things on the Thanksgiving table that people have stronger opinions about than gravy. Everyone seems to have a preferred method, a secret ingredient or a little trick they’ve been using for years. My mom has always sworn by Kitchen Bouquet, a seasoning sauce that gives gravy a little color and kick of flavor. I’m fairly certain she’s had the same bottle since the Reagan administration, and that it only comes out of the cupboard on Thanksgiving.

According to recent reports, making good turkey gravy isn’t particularly complicated, but getting that deep, rich flavor can be tricky. Even with plenty of turkey drippings and a well-made stock, sometimes it needs a little something extra. Over the years, I’ve experimented with all sorts of ways to give my gravy more flavor, but the one I come back to every time is an ingredient I always have in my pantry.

I’ve been adding a splash of soy sauce to my gravy for years, and it’s one of those little tricks that makes a noticeable difference without anyone being able to put their finger on why.

Soy sauce is rich in umami, the deeply savory flavor that makes foods like mushrooms, Parmesan cheese and the golden crust of a steak so satisfying. Adding a little soy sauce to gravy enhances those same savory flavors, giving it a richness that might otherwise require a longer cooking time. It doesn’t make your gravy taste like soy sauce, provided you use a light hand. It just makes it taste more like really good gravy.

Worcestershire sauce is another popular addition that works for much the same reason, bringing its own combination of savory flavor, acidity and a hint of sweetness. I’ve tried plenty of different additions over the years, and while they all have their merits, soy sauce remains my favorite. I love the depth it brings without competing with the flavors of the turkey and stock.

Industry observers note that the trick with soy sauce is knowing when to add it and, perhaps most importantly, when to stop. You’re not trying to introduce a newly introduced flavor to your gravy so much as coax a little more out of what’s already there. If someone can identify soy sauce in the finished product, you’ve probably been a bit too generous.

I always add mine at the end, once the gravy has thickened and I’m happy with the consistency. Start with about a teaspoon for every two cups of gravy, stir it in, and give it a taste. Depending on the stock and drippings you’ve used, that may be all you need. If not, add a little more, tasting as you go.

One thing worth remembering is that soy sauce is salty. Very salty, in fact, so save your final seasoning adjustments until after you’ve added it. This is particularly vital if you’re using store-bought stock, which may already contain plenty of sodium. Reduced-sodium soy sauce is an option, too, but I generally use the regular stuff and adjust accordingly.

And don’t save this trick for Thanksgiving! It works beautifully in beef and chicken gravy, too, especially when the pan drippings aren’t quite as flavorful as you’d hoped. A splash of soy sauce won’t make up for a badly made gravy, but it can do an impressive amount of work for an otherwise perfectly respectable one.

Have you used soy sauce in gravy before? Let us know in the comments below!

The New Rules for Selling Beauty in China

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2260 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that since Yang Zifeng and Zhou Tiancheng launched Flower Knows in 2016, the Chinese beauty brand has captured the local market with its ultra-feminine, fairytale-inspired aesthetic.
  • This May marked a upcoming chapter for Flower Knows, which sold a majority stake to Proya Cosmetics as part of a RMB 351 million (roughly $52.6 million) deal — a move that reflects how far C-beauty has come, for both the acquired and the acquirer.
  • Founded in 2003, Proya began as a single skincare brand, offering proven active ingredients at accessible prices to China’s lower-tier cities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that since Yang Zifeng and Zhou Tiancheng launched Flower Knows in 2016, the Chinese beauty brand has captured the local market with its ultra-feminine, fairytale-inspired aesthetic. Think whimsical collections of lip glosses, blushes, and eye palettes that favor softer, buildable colors and sheerer applications, drawing on the duo’s passion for cosplay — for which they have built a sizable following in China under the stage names Baozi and Hana.

This May marked a upcoming chapter for Flower Knows, which sold a majority stake to Proya Cosmetics as part of a RMB 351 million (roughly $52.6 million) deal — a move that reflects how far C-beauty has come, for both the acquired and the acquirer.

Founded in 2003, Proya began as a single skincare brand, offering proven active ingredients at accessible prices to China’s lower-tier cities. It expanded into a multi-brand group in the late 2010s – anchored by its 2017 IPO listing and 2019 acquisition of the Chinese makeup brand Timage. In 2024, Proya surpassed RMB 10 billion ($1 billion) in annual revenue, making it China’s largest beauty tech giant.

Proya’s decision to acquire Flower Knows highlights its strategy to buy rather than build, as it diversifies beyond its flagship skincare brand of the same name. The group first invested in Flower Knows last August and, in May, acquired an additional stake, raising its total ownership to 51%. The move is part of Proya’s ambitious initiative to become one of the top 10 global cosmetics companies by 2035, with a target of RMB 50 billion ($7.5 billion) in annual revenue. Proya’s stock jumped 5.1% on the Shanghai Stock Exchange following the announcement.

Yang Zifeng and Zhou Tiancheng launched Flower Knows in 2016.

Proya’s aim represents a bigger shift for the market. China’s beauty landscape over the past decade has evolved from low-cost dupes of Western and Korean cosmetics into a value-driven, culturally distinct global powerhouse capable of commanding serious valuations. Now, having secured majority market share at home, many C-beauty brands are setting their sights on overseas expansion and are moving past social media buzz into controlled offline retail channels to build long-term profitability and trust.

In a recent development, “Over the past decade, we’ve built a distinct creative identity and a passionate community. At the same time, we recognize that the beauty market is becoming more competitive and consumers are more selective about where they spend,” claims Flower Knows’s global CMO Fang Gongyiliu. “That makes it even more important to invest in product innovation, operational efficiency, and sustainable brand building, rather than relying on short-term trends. Our ambition isn’t simply to become a bigger brand, but to become a more enduring one.”.

China is the world’s second‐largest consumer market for cosmetics. The latest data from the National Bureau of Statistics of China shows that cosmetics retail sales in September 2026 generated RMB 39 billion ($5.85 billion), up 5.4% year-on-year. Meanwhile, cosmetic retail sales in the country between January and September 2026 totaled RMB 349 billion ($20.9 billion), up 6.1% compared to the same period in 2025.

Driving the sector are multinational legacy brands, such as Chanel Beauty, La Mer and L’Oréal (the group’s business in mainland China returned to growth in late 2025 and continued its momentum into 2026), and rapidly surging domestic players, like Proya, Florasis and Maogeping, which collectively command more than half the domestic market, according to the China Association of Fragrance, Flavor and Cosmetic Industries.

Hua Mantian and Freeman Ren co-launched Florasis, selling cosmetics infused with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) concepts and local craftsmanship and aesthetics.

And while K-beauty has taken the world by storm, surpassing the US to become the second-largest beauty exporter globally, Chinese consumers have generally shown little interest. It’s in part due to historical geopolitical tensions that resulted in unofficial restrictions starting in 2016 on South Korean cultural and consumer goods. K-beauty’s market share in China has fallen sharply from 66% to 20%, according to 2025 Euromonitor data. In recent years, Korean beauty conglomerate Amorepacific reported that its North American business had overtaken its China revenue.

Recent findings suggest that china operates as a self-contained ecosystem distinct from Western or other Asian markets. In the latter, shoppers tend to rely heavily on physical stores like Sephora or Olive Young for product discovery and hands-on testing. China’s retail ecosystem, on the other hand, is built around native, digitally integrated super-apps, such as Baidu (China’s dominant search engine), Douyin and Xiaohongshu (which play a central role in brand discovery and reviews); transaction hubs like Taobao, Tmall, JD.com and even discount site Pinduoduo; and WeChat and Alipay (which combine messaging and mobile payments, as cash and traditional credit cards are rarely used).

“The Chinese consumer is probably not seeing all these ads on Medicube or the other dozen beauty brands that are doing very well globally,” states Cherrie Rao, a former marketing executive who recently relocated to the US after living in Beijing and Shanghai for the past decade.

Thus, local visibility is crucial. That’s why most C-beauty players start online. In 2017, when Hua Mantian and Freeman Ren co-introduced Florasis, selling cosmetics infused with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) concepts and local craftsmanship and aesthetics, they bypassed traditional brick-and-mortar retail, focusing primarily on DTC distribution via local platforms like Tmall. Flower Knows has also sold primarily through digital platforms like Taobao, where it frequently hosts livestream broadcasts and ranks among top category sellers. But reaching Chinese consumers requires more than just local platform integration.

In a recent development, “Over the past decade, we’ve learned that storytelling alone isn’t enough to build a lasting beauty brand,” states Flower Knows’s Fang. “We often say that our products are the most important form of content. The intricate packaging, colors, textures, and the experience of opening a product give our consumers something worth discovering and sharing… But how it performs and how it fits into their everyday routine is what helps turn that interest into a purchase.”.

Florasis’s key is connecting with consumers beyond recognizable aesthetics. “‘Eastern elegance’ is more than a visual style. It represents a contemporary way of living”, a spokesperson tells Vogue Business. Indeed, while consumers in China are not a monolith and span vastly different regions and thus experiences and preferences, they share a cultural foundation — including an extraordinarily rich tradition of proverbs and idioms — that continues to deeply shape people’s moral values, social behavior and daily choices.

In a recent development, “I think the companies who are [driving] cultural confidence are the ones who are truly living the philosophy behind Chinese culture as well,” says Jess Tang, the founder of Dumpling, an Asia-focused brand strategy and design practice, and former head of Asia insights at forecasting firm WGSN. In C-beauty, this requires a real commitment to the community, she explains. “They’re building a business that is not just about making money, but is giving back to their country, to their hometown, to the villagers.”.

Chinese fragrance houses like To Summer and Documents have built entire sensory worlds around cultural traditions and objects. Since launching in Beijing in 2018, To Summer has worked directly with local farmers to extract native botanicals like Jingmai Pu’er tea, Hubei osmanthus and Xinhui tangerine peel. Its retail spaces are often set inside restored historic courtyards and heritage buildings featuring Jingdezhen porcelain and traditional craft. Founded in Shanghai in 2021, Documents reinterprets not only traditional incense but also historical Chinese scent-wearing traditions, using knotted bag charms for its 5ml perfumes (instead of standard spray bottles).

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the C-beauty brand Maogeping Cosmetics has become a national success story since its launch in 2000 by the namesake makeup artist. Widely celebrated as China’s first homegrown luxury beauty brand, Maogeping broke a decades-long monopoly held by Western and Japanese cosmetics giants in China’s high-end department stores and culminated its 24-year rise with a landmark HK$2.3 billion (about $300 million) IPO in Hong Kong in December 2024, turning its founder into a billionaire. Strong momentum has continued following its listing, with the organization reporting 2025 full-year revenues of RMB 5.1 billion ($757 million), up 30% year-over-year.

In a recent development, at the heart of Maogeping’s approach is education. While most beauty brands in China prioritize e-commerce, Mao invested in hundreds of department store counters across China, using these sites not simply as points of sale but as beauty studios where trained consultants offered personalized makeup lessons and demonstrations. The manufacturer also runs its own school, teaching makeup artistry, styling, and image design, across 11 cities in China, including Beijing, Hangzhou, Chongqing and Wuhan. In Tang’s view, this contributes to the local ecosystem. “I find that powerful because, from an Asian perspective, you have to give back as much in order to grow.”.

Riding the wave of cultural pride — dubbed the “guochao” movement, where Chinese millennials and Gen Z actively support domestic brands — has helped C-beauty brands to bypass the slower growth typical of latest companies.

Sources indicate that but beyond growing national confidence, there has also been a major leap in the quality, design and innovation of C-beauty products over the past decade. Western or Korean brands simply “cannot keep up”, says Linda Yu, the general manager of Red Ant Asia, which advises global brands including Creed, Moncler, Charlotte Tilbury and Byredo on navigating China’s digital landscape and overseas retailers on which C-beauty labels to stock.

Rather than copying Western formulas, domestic companies such as Giant Biogene and Bloomage Biotech (which has backed Rao’s newly debuted brand, Alaris) invest heavily in proprietary R&D. Florasis, Flower Knows and Perfect Diary have turned packaging into collectible art. And brands including Judydoll (with its metal-wand “curling iron” mascara), Joocyee (for its high-performance lip formulas and jelly highlighters) and Winona (whose formulations are tailored to sensitive skin) have invented viral, functional products that Western competitors struggle to match.

Brands such as Joocyee, known for its high-performance lip formulas and jelly highlighters, have invented viral, functional products that Western competitors struggle to match.

Among C-beauty’s bright spots are color cosmetics, fragrance and beauty tools, of which online sales, tracked from January to September 2025, rose 5.4% to RMB 94.7 billion ($14.2 billion), compared to skincare, which remains the dominant category but fell 0.8% to RMB 207.8 billion ($31.2 billion), according to the latest data from Moojing, a Beijing-based consumer intelligence platform that tracks online sales across APAC.

However, amid China’s wider economic slowdown, “the overall guochao halo is fading,” warns Yu – not because Chinese consumers are returning to foreign brands, but because surface-level patriotism is no longer enough to sell a product. Thus, she notes, “distinctiveness” remains key. Ellie Thorpe, director at intelligence firm Kantar BrandZ, agrees, noting that the strongest players in China compete on a point of view and give customers “a clear reason to choose them”.

Sources indicate that brands must also contend with changing beauty standards. While a fair, youthful and highly filtered look — coined by locals as 网红脸 wang hong lian, or “influencer face” — has long been the dominant beauty aesthetic, experts say this ideal is declining in favor of natural body types, healthy complexion and “no makeup” makeup. “I think beauty standards are becoming more diverse,” notes Rao, attributing the shift to the influx of K-pop and American culture on apps like Xiaohongshu. “There are now women who want to have sun-kissed skin or draw on freckles. They want to look healthy and natural.”.

Amid shifting consumer sentiment and intensifying local competition, domestic brands are also looking to offline retail channels, including overseas, for newly introduced pockets of growth. This indicates their ambition to compete on sustainable new customer acquisition and retention, rather than aggressive discounting via major local shopping events like Double 11 (also known as Singles’ Day), 520, Golden Week, and Qixi. Instead of chasing one-time bargain hunters, the focus now is on converting buyers into high-value repeat customers through prestige counters and mainstream retail partnerships.

From heritage festivals to digital shopping bonanzas, 2025 presents several opportunities to engage with China’s fast-changing market.

Florasis opened its first flagship in Hangzhou in 2022 and its first overseas store in Tokyo in 2025. Today, it is stocked by retailers in over 110 countries and regions, including Samaritaine Paris Pont Neuf in Paris, Skin Cupid in London, and Mall of the Emirates in Dubai. Meanwhile, Flower Knows expanded to Boots in the UK this March and physical Ulta stores in the US as of September. At home, it has entered specialty retailers such as Wow Colour (China’s answer to Sephora) and, in October, opened its first global flagship store on Huaihai Middle Road in Shanghai. China remains Flower Knows’s largest market overall, but the US has become its biggest internationally, Fang indicates.

Whether C-beauty can build lasting recognition outside of its home country remains to be seen.

But ultimately, the industry’s glow-up points to a bigger change, one where China is no longer a low-cost manufacturer and imitator, but a global powerhouse driven by original science, intricate design and innovation. See, for example, adjacent consumer industries like automobiles: China now leads the global EV industry, producing a majority of the world's electric cars and even collaborating with top European fashion figures like Kim Jones.

According to recent reports, “The idea is that the Chinese population should be creating things that are our own instead of mimicking trends in Korea or elsewhere, whether it’s politics or culture,” states Rao. “I see a shift where China has gone from being the world’s factory to becoming the world’s lab.”.

In a recent development, stephen Miller, White House deputy chief of staff, talks with reporters at the White House on April 28. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

President Donald Trump on Friday announced that Stephen Miller, the architect of the hard-line immigration and deportation program voters rejected this week, will become White House chief of staff.

According to recent reports, susie Wiles will depart that post and move to the Trump political organization, which appears to be in full operation, even after the president's last midterm election. Miller has been deputy chief of staff, overseeing the Trump administration's domestic policy.

Miller’s first day will be Monday, Trump remarked in a social media post.

Trump dubbed Miller “one of my most trusted advisors” and mentioned Wiles, who also oversaw his 2024 presidential campaign, “has done an outstanding job.”.

Wiles, who Trump recently announced had won a battle with breast cancer, said in a X post that “serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime,” adding she was “proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”.

The chief-of-staff change came three days after Republicans were demolished in Trump’s final midterm election, with House Democrats on pace for the largest majority in over a decade and at least a 54-seat Senate majority come January.

Trump addressed the personnel move as he departed the White House Friday for an event and weekend in Florida — though he ignored a question about his recent declaration that Wiles would be sticking around.

“I wanted to make a change,” he said in a roughly three-minute exchange with reporters before he walked to Marine One. “Sometimes in life, you have to make moves.”.

It has been revealed that trump in recent days had become open to working with Democrats after the new Congress is seated on Jan. 3, even after railing against what he called the party’s “bad” policy during an October-long campaign rally blitz.

It has been revealed that “Look, I mean, I'll get along, probably, with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive,” Trump told reporters Wednesday. “But I have the power of the veto. So if we don't like what they're doing… They've already called and they want to talk about things. And that's fine.”.

Trump summoned Thursday's press pool into the Oval Office for an executive order signing. On his desk was a red baseball cap with "VETO" across the front in large white lettering.

Sources indicate that miller has worked on Capitol Hill as an aide to several GOP lawmakers, including former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who became attorney general in Trump's first administration.

But making the hard-line Miller his White House chief of staff even before congressional Democrats get organized likely will draw the ire of the incoming majority.

Virginia Rep. Donald S. Beyer Jr. was among the first Democratic lawmakers to slam Trump’s decision.

Recent findings suggest that “Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller doubles down on the politics of hatred, lawlessness, and failure that the American people soundly rejected three days ago,” Beyer said in a statement. "Miller embodies the worst elements of the Trump presidency. His promotion indicates that Trump has learned nothing from his electoral debacle and has no intention of even trying to work constructively with the next Congress.”.

Many congressional Democrats — leaders, returning incumbents and members-elect — want to investigate Trump, his inner circle and family members while also pursuing a legislative agenda aimed at paring the cost of living.

To that end, as chief of staff, Democrat-run committees calling Miller to testify is highly unlikely since he could continue to claim executive privilege. That allows senior White House aides to withhold many internal West Wing communications, documents, and presidential-related conversations and actions, from lawmakers.

In public comments and television interviews, Miller has accused Democrats of being aligned with figures and candidates who “hate” Americans, and once mentioned the party is “unworthy of power.”.

Recent findings suggest that “So the Democrats have become a party of freaks, weirdos, losers and crazies,” Miller said during a July appearance on Fox News. “But you can’t laugh it off because it’s deadly serious. When you give these people power, everything you know and love in this world falls apart. You have chaos, corruption, decay, violence, poverty.”.
